summary: Ontonagon County, MI Ottawa National Forest lookout built circa 1938, torn down by 1975; register lists a 2024 survey reference mark photo at the site.

facts.status_note: Torn down by 1975 per a later survey noted on the register; the register describes only a survey reference mark at the site (photo dated September 2024)

events.note: Register gives circa 1938; the exact build date is unknown; a survey spike at the site is stamped 1938

Newspaper item (quoted on a Houghton County lookout page): bids to remove ten Ottawa National Forest towers; a quoted fragment mentions a tower located on Paulding, which does not clearly match this site
Torn down by 1975, as noted in a later survey
Registered January 1, 2026; nominated by Kenneth McDonough

evidence.supports: built circa 1938 with exact date unknown; site first marked by survey in 1939; spike stamped 1938
evidence.quote: The exact date built is unknown, but the site was first marked by survey in 1939, noting that the spike in the ground was stamped 1938.

evidence.supports: torn down by 1975 as noted in a later survey
evidence.quote: As is the case for many towers, the tower was torn down by 1975 as noted in a later survey.

evidence.quote: Pauling Reference Mark #1 in September 2024 - courtesy of Kenneth McDonough

evidence.quote: Bids for the removal of ten fire towers have been sent out to interested parties, according to an announcement by Joseph Harn, Supervisor of the Ottawa National Forest.

corrections.why: The register's Built field says circa 1938 and its description says the exact date is unknown

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The photo caption on the register page spells the reference mark Pauling; the register title and location use Paulding. The story uses Paulding and quotes the caption as printed.

notes_for_editor: Construction and removal dates rest on one register page. A search for a second source (build, staffing or use) found nothing usable; the Michigan Tech fire tower page has no Paulding entry, and the Paulding Light is a folklore phenomenon, not this site. The 1971 item on the Conners page may or may not refer to this tower, and the story says so. No staffing, fire history, height or design is in any source read, so none is given. A lead for an editor: Ottawa National Forest headquarters in Ironwood for tower records.
